optical.description: High-resolution visible spectrum orbital imagery used for boulder field mapping, sand ripple traversability, and visual verification of polygonal ridges.
optical.caveat: Optical imagery cannot measure subsurface cohesion or bearing capacity without ground truth.

elevation.description: Digital elevation model referenced to the Mars Datum (areoid), measuring absolute topography and cumulative climb/descent.
elevation.caveat: Interpolated regional DTMs may smooth out sub-meter vertical drop-offs and crevices.

slope.description: First-derivative terrain gradient expressed in degrees. 0-5° flat, 5-12° gentle, 12-20° steep, >20° extreme/no-go.
slope.caveat: Averaged over 50m baselines; micro-slopes on boulders or ridge scarps can be substantially steeper.

thermal.description: Orbital thermal infrared brightness temperature and derived thermal inertia (J m^-2 K^-1 s^-1/2), distinguishing cemented duricrust/bedrock (>300 units) from loose drift dust (<150 units).
thermal.caveat: MANDATORY CAVEAT: Orbital thermal inertia reflects surface thermal property and density; it is NOT a live surface weather or temperature forecast.

mineralogy.description: Hyperspectral visible/near-infrared reflectance spectroscopy detecting diagnostic absorption bands of polyhydrated sulfates, smectite clays, and crystalline hematite.
mineralogy.caveat: Affected by atmospheric dust dust-cover and shadows; in-situ spectroscopic ground-truthing is required.

radiation.resolution: In-situ point detector on rover deck
radiation.description: Historical surface measurements of Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and solar particle doses (~25.2 μSv/hr nominal baseline).
radiation.caveat: MANDATORY CAVEAT: Historical surface measurements provide baseline environmental context, but do NOT establish future human astronaut exposure or predict acute Solar Particle Events.
